summary: onsaleFull discards all evidence when any stage aborts — defer writeReport
description:
### Finding (TKT-125 measurement, 2026-07-27)

`writeReport(t, report)` is the **last statement** of `onsaleFull` (`smoke/onsale_load_test.go`). Every `generatorHealthy` check is a `t.Fatalf`, so a single aborted stage discards the whole accumulated `report` — including stages that completed cleanly minutes earlier.

This cost TKT-125 its COS: on a single-host setup the ceiling sweep's `sweep-600` stage trips the generator guard **every time** (3 runs of 3, on 4-9 client-side transport errors at 600 attempts/s), so no JSON was ever emitted, even though the `nfr-3000pm` stage the ticket actually needed had completed 9,000/9,000 clean. `finalize_p99_ms` and `confirm_p99_ms` exist only in that report, so they could not be recorded.

### Scope

`defer writeReport(t, report)` (or equivalent) so a partial run still emits what it measured. The report already carries per-stage entries appended as they complete, so partial output is meaningful, not misleading — but consider marking the report `partial: true` so a reader cannot mistake an aborted run for a complete one.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An `onsaleFull` run whose sweep aborts still writes `ONSALE_REPORT` containing every completed stage
- [ ] The report distinguishes complete from partial runs
- [ ] TKT-125's missing `finalize_p99_ms` / `confirm_p99_ms` are obtainable by re-running the two arms
- [ ] `make check` green

objective.note: An aborted stage discards every stage that already completed; TKT-125 lost finalize_p99_ms/confirm_p99_ms to it.

scope.note: IN: defer writeReport + a partial marker in smoke/onsale_load_test.go. OUT: re-running the ceiling sweep to harvest TKT-125s numbers, and any change to the generatorHealthy guard itself.

uncertainties.note: Only whether a partial report can mislead a reader — closed by the partial marker (AC 2). t.Fatalf runs deferred functions, so defer is sufficient; no goroutine-exit path in onsaleFull bypasses it.

dependencies.note: None. smoke/onsale_load_test.go is untouched by anything in flight.

approach.note: defer writeReport(t, report) at the top of onsaleFull (currently the last statement, :519) + report.partial set true unless the run reaches the end.

first_slice.note: One function, one defer, one field. Whole ticket is the slice.

success.note: AC 3 resolved to mechanism-only (see readiness comment) — an injected abort proves the completed stages survive; harvesting TKT-125s numbers is a separate run, not this diff.

context_memo.note: No ADR governs the smoke load harness reporting format — checked all of docs/adr/ at HEAD. ADR-030 is the catalog coverage gate, not this. Recorded as a finding, not an omission.

### DoR — 8/8 (1 deferred). Shaped 2026-07-28.

**Decision taken at shaping (owner call, delegated):** AC 3 is **mechanism-only**. The ticket
delivers "a partial report survives an aborted sweep"; it does **not** require re-running the
ceiling sweep to actually record TKT-125's `finalize_p99_ms` / `confirm_p99_ms`. Reason: on a
single-host setup `sweep-600` trips the generator guard every time (3/3 runs), so binding this
diff to a green full run binds it to a host it cannot have. Rewrite AC 3 as: *an `onsaleFull`
run aborted at `sweep-600` writes a report containing the `nfr-3000pm` stage's
`finalize_p99_ms` and `confirm_p99_ms`* — provable by an injected abort in seconds.

`context_memo` is `deferred`, not skipped: no ADR governs the load harness's reporting. Checked
docs/adr/ at HEAD; the nearest candidate (ADR-030) is the catalog coverage gate.

**Verdict: READY.** `risk:low` stands — one `defer`, one bool, no source outside `smoke/`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — authored by **gpt-5.6-sol** (`config.models.plan`), effort high, read-only

Run via the codex companion `task` command, no `--write`. Verbatim below; critique follows in
`kind=plan-final`.

---

## DoD

- `onsaleFull` writes `ONSALE_REPORT` from a deferred path whenever reporting has begun, including after `t.Fatalf`.
- An aborted run contains every previously accepted stage; specifically, `nfr-3000pm` retains `finalize_p99_ms` and `confirm_p99_ms`.
- Every new report explicitly contains `"partial": true` after an abort and `"partial": false` after normal completion.
- The aborting `sweep-600` stage remains excluded because `generatorHealthy` runs before its append (`smoke/onsale_load_test.go:474-480`); invalid generator evidence must not be published.
- `generatorHealthy` is unchanged.
- The normal `make check` gate passes. No real ceiling sweep is run for this ticket.

## Plan

1. Add `Partial bool \`json:"partial"\`` to `loadtest.Report` at `smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest.go:312-329`. Do not use `omitempty`, so complete reports explicitly serialize `false`.

2. Add a small reporting-lifecycle helper near `writeReport` (`smoke/onsale_load_test.go:250-263`) that:

   - Sets `report.Partial = true`.
   - Defers `writeReport(t, report)`.
   - Invokes the supplied profile body synchronously.
   - Sets `report.Partial = false` only after that body returns normally.

   Wrap the existing `onsaleFull` body with this helper. Keep the stage order and `generatorHealthy` closure (`:409-418`) unchanged. The NFR report is already appended before the sweep (`:430-441`), and its percentile fields originate at `smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest.go:289-304`.

3. Apply the same helper to `onsaleGate`, replacing its terminal write at `smoke/onsale_load_test.go:391`. It has the identical loss mode after appending stages (`:303-342`) and shares the same report schema; profile-dependent semantics would be surprising.

4. Add the regression tests described below, then run `make check`.

## Test seam

Add `smoke/onsale_load_report_test.go` with the `smoke` build tag.

- Complete-path test: set `ONSALE_REPORT` to `t.TempDir()`, invoke the reporting helper with a callback that returns normally, parse the JSON, and assert the `partial` key is present and `false`.
- Abort-path test: execute the current test binary as a subprocess with an environment sentinel and temporary `ONSALE_REPORT`. In child mode, invoke the same reporting helper; append a synthetic `nfr-3000pm` `StageReport` with distinct `FinalizeP99Ms` and `ConfirmP99Ms`, then call `t.Fatalf("injected abort at sweep-600")`.
- The parent must assert:

  - The subprocess exits non-zero for the expected injected diagnostic.
  - The JSON file exists and parses.
  - `partial` is explicitly `true`.
  - `nfr-3000pm` exists with the exact injected finalize/confirm p99 values.

The subprocess is necessary because an expected `t.Fatal` cannot be neutralized by a subtest: it permanently fails its parent test. The deferred writer still receives a real `*testing.T`; any writer failure therefore remains a genuine child failure.

This test runs in the normal gate because `make check` includes `smoke` (`Makefile:17,102-107`), and the smoke script runs the package without an allowlist (`scripts/smoke.sh:190-199`). The injected body uses no database, HTTP, or timed load and completes in seconds.

## Files touched

- `smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest.go` — add the serialized `Partial` field.
- `smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest_test.go` — extend the existing JSON metadata coverage at `:329-354` to pin the explicit `partial` key.
- `smoke/onsale_load_test.go` — add the deferred lifecycle helper; route both profiles through it; remove both terminal `writeReport` calls.
- `smoke/onsale_load_report_test.go` — add normal-return and subprocess-fatal regression tests.

## DECISION: partial marker

Options are an explicit boolean or a completion-status enum.

Recommendation: `Partial bool \`json:"partial"\``. It is the smallest additive format change and matches the ticket language. Set it `true` before entering the run and clear it only on normal return.

Trade-off: older reports omit the field, and decoding them directly into a Go `bool` yields `false`. Readers must treat a missing key as legacy/unknown—not proof of completion. A status enum would preserve that distinction automatically but adds unnecessary schema and consumer complexity for this ticket.

## Control-flow finding and risks

There is no current goroutine-exit path around the defer. `RunStage` launches workers but waits for all of them before returning (`smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest.go:109-147`); workers return `Outcome` values and never receive `*testing.T`. All `generatorHealthy` calls and other fatal checks execute synchronously on the test goroutine.

Risks:

- `partial:false` means the profile reached its end, not that every nonfatal assertion passed; `t.Errorf` should still produce a complete report.
- `os.Exit`, `SIGKILL`, a process crash, or an unwritable report path cannot be rescued by a defer.
- The callback/helper extraction must remain synchronous; moving the profile body into a goroutine would invalidate the guarantee.
- Do not move the failed sweep append ahead of `generatorHealthy`; that would publish explicitly inconclusive evidence.
